Each entry stores the SOURCE TEXT it was judged against: if that line is edited or shifts, the report emits 'unclassified-stale' instead of carrying the judgement onto changed code. _instrument_line_attribution_warning: MEASURED 2026-08-11, and it invalidates the CLAUSE NAMED in any judgement on a multi-line || chain: at -O0 gcov attributes each clause's branch to the line BEFORE it. Proven by running inputs in isolation and counting -- four 'been running' inputs produced a true-count of exactly 4 on the line holding 'been up' (route.c:268), while route.c:269 ('been running') showed outcomes totalling exactly the 5 inputs that fell through to the next clause. So a report naming ':269 rt_seq2(been,running)' is really naming 'been on' (line 270), and ':296 (... day is ...)' is really naming 'date is' (line 297). Two judgements below were written against the quoted text and therefore named the wrong clause; aiming at the quoted clause covers a different line and leaves the reported gap open, which reads exactly like the directed case not working. The LINE NUMBER is reliable; the SOURCE TEXT beside it may belong to the next clause down.

judgements.source_at_judgement: for (size_t i = 0; i < len && o + 1 < norm_size; i++) {
judgements.reason: The never-taken outcome is the WRITE BOUND (`o + 1 < norm_size` false) -- the truncation guard on an untrusted-input buffer. The RAW fuzz mode already feeds 0..256 bytes (fuzz_query_shield.c:145), so it exceeds the 192 buffer and is TRYING to reach this; it fails on statistics, not on structure. MEASURED: a random 256-byte stream normalises to mean 108.5 / max 145 over 2000 samples, against a write bound of 191 -- only ~24% of random byte values are alnum and every non-alnum run collapses to a single space. A 220-byte all-alnum input reaches the bound immediately (verified, no crash). One additional fuzz mode emitting long alphanumeric runs would cover it. Deployed callers cap at CONTROL_QUERY_MAX=172 so this is not a live defect, but it is the write-bound guard and it is currently unexercised.
